en: Vimānavatthu:
Purisavimāna,
Pāyāsivagga
8. The First Kuṇḍalī Vimāna Story “Adorned,
wearing garlands, well-dressed,
with beautiful earrings and hair and beard trimmed;”
Famous, with hand-ornaments fastened on,
he dwells in a celestial mansion like the moon;
and divine lutes play a lovely melody.
Well-trained and of noble form,
groups of eight by eight celestial maidens who roam among the Thirty-three gods dance, sing, and bring delight.
You have attained divine power and possess great majesty;
while still a human being, what merit did you perform?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing splendor?
"And your radiance illuminates all directions.
That son of the gods, being delighted... [as before]...
The fruit of which deed is this:
"Having been born as a human among humans,
I saw ascetics endowed with virtue."
To one who has perfected true knowledge and conduct,
who is renowned, learned, and established in the destruction of craving— to such a person,
with a mind full of serene faith, [one should offer] food and drink.
I gave abundant gifts with due respect.
Because of that, such is my complexion... [and so on].
"And my radiance shines in all directions.
Thus ends the eighth, the First Kuṇḍalī-vimāna.
